title: Data Binding Model
description: Connects a component's declared data role to a field of a named data source. Bindings are the seam between the component contract (which roles exist) and the data model (which fields exist), and they are validated against both — the manifest supplies required roles, the data source supplies available aliases.

bindingSet.description: All bindings for one component instance, keyed by the role names its manifest declares. Repeated roles such as grid columns or chart series take an array.

source.description: Data source id declared on the page. Omitted when the component instance declares a default dataSource and this binding uses it.

field.description: Alias from the data source's select clause. Referencing the alias rather than the catalog attribute means a steward can re-point an attribute without touching component configuration.

label.description: Display label override. Defaults to the data source field label, which defaults to the catalog business name — so a generated page is correctly labelled without the generator inventing text.

transform.description: Pure display transform over the bound value. Not a substitute for a catalog measure: anything reusable or business-meaningful belongs in the catalog where it can be governed.

thresholds.description: Overrides the measure's defaultThresholds for this binding only.

width.description: Column width hint, for tabular roles.

hidden.description: Bound but not displayed. Used to carry a key needed by a drill-down action without showing it.

action.description: Action invoked when this field is activated — the mechanism that makes an identifier column a drill-down link.

renderAs.description: Presentation hint within the bound cell. Constrained to a closed set so a definition cannot smuggle in arbitrary markup, which would be an injection surface.

encodingBinding.description: Chart encoding: maps a data field to a visual channel. Modelling charts as mark plus encodings, rather than as a family of near-duplicate component types, gives the generation service a compositional vocabulary — choose a mark, map fields to channels — instead of a choice among twenty similar components.
